scenes.focusTo: Headline centre, handing off to the workspace
scenes.purpose: Open on a plain goal so the film starts from work, not from a feature list.
Land the real MiniMax Code screen at rest so every later line rests on actual product material.
Turn the single goal into ordered steps across real interface regions: input, task chips, Projects list.

scenes.focusTo: Claims header and two attributed cards
scenes.purpose: Name the described modes and agent teamwork, framed explicitly as MiniMax's own product claims, not measured results, in two cards wide enough for their real interface crops and labels to read.
Resolve on the single call to action with room to read the label and URL.

claims-header.text: Product claims, as MiniMax describes them

treatment.continuity: One screenshot carries the whole middle: the full workspace lands, then the camera moves through its own regions (input, task chips, Projects) as ordered steps, so the goal visibly travels through the product. The claims section is trimmed to two cards so each carries a real interface crop at a readable size next to its short label, preventing the thin empty-shell cards and cramped text of the previous cut; both crops reuse the same product regions as the step sequence. Each transition overlaps the outgoing scene by its transition length. Light bg and ink from the interface stay constant; the interface blue is the only accent, used for the active step and the CTA. Every claim card sits under an attribution header so product statements are never read as independent results. Internal evaluation only; asset and copy are not cleared for public render.

holds.reason: Hook headline reads at rest before the workspace crossfades in.
Real interface and its label settle long enough to register.
Attribution header and two cards need a full reading hold without cramping.
CTA and URL hold to the final frame.

treatment.message: A plain goal meets the real MiniMax Code workspace and becomes steps; the Coding and Work modes and agents teaming up stay framed as MiniMax's own product claims, never as measured results.
